result: Runtime provenance is now an explicit forward-only scientific authorization predicate rather than post-hoc metadata. Historical ADMITs are not reinterpreted. New ADMITs bind the frozen reservation-runtime dependency digest before score generation; matching RESERVE provenance is required by the superseding auditor, and a contracted ADMIT cannot downgrade to the historical compliance CLOSE path. A 4531-byte-cut injected lifecycle preserved fail-closed semantics from ADMIT through restart. Separately, a POSIX flock + whole-file CAS + fsync/readback writer serialized 832 competing process attempts across 41 races with exactly one winner per race and rejected all stale prefixes.
validated_contracts: Historical blocks without the new pre-score contract retain their historical scientific acceptance predicate; provenance differences alone do not retroactively invalidate exact attempt evidence.
For new contracted blocks, missing or mismatched RESERVE runtime provenance fails closed because the condition was fixed in ADMIT before any score could be generated.
A contracted ADMIT cannot be closed through the historical reservation-compliance binding; replay rejects that downgrade path while preserving replay of genuinely historical CLOSE events.

Across 4531 nonempty partial-frame cuts spanning ADMIT, RESERVE, SLOT, COMMIT and CLOSE, torn evidence was never treated as a clean complete append; missing COMMIT remained reconcilable from durable SLOT identity without a second scorer invocation; torn CLOSE produced zero reporting rows.

Single-host cooperative cross-process appends can be serialized without changing scientific event semantics by holding POSIX flock across exact whole-file CAS, append, fsync and exact readback. In 41 races / 832 process attempts there was exactly one successful append per race and 791 CAS rejections.
A crash-like partial append is not silently crossed by the flocked writer: subsequent append sees a prefix mismatch and fails until recovery truncates/quarantines to a validated prefix.
measurement_validity_rules: Do not turn provenance metadata into a new scientific acceptance rule after evidence exists. Bind any provenance requirement before scoring, then enforce it mechanically at CLOSE/replay.

Authorization provenance and scientific identity remain distinct: reservation payload/digest and attempt_id retain scientific identity; runtime binding proves which authorized path emitted the reservation.
A forward contract must be downgrade-resistant: once ADMIT opts into a stronger predicate, historical CLOSE/replay cannot be used to bypass it.

Crash validity and concurrency validity are separate. Append-frame crash tests do not prove simultaneous writer safety; a reliable exclusion primitive plus CAS/readback is required for cooperative multi-process writers.

Cross-file atomicity is not required for the main journal and reservation ledger because existing partial-order recovery deliberately treats incomplete cross-file transitions as fail-closed/reconcilable states.
scope_limitations: The provenance full-chain campaign used deterministic contract-faithful injected interfaces with the persisted event fields and frame codec; the exact complete frozen production sibling graph was not byte-executed in one repository-local checkout.

The flocked writer result is single-host/cooperative only on filesystems with reliable POSIX flock semantics. It is not a distributed lease/fencing proof for NFS, object stores or multi-host writers, and it cannot constrain callers that bypass the writer.

The full-chain crash campaign and the cross-process writer race were validated separately; a single campaign combining actual provenance runtime transitions with multiple racing OS processes remains outstanding.
No conclusion extends beyond the tested durability, authorization-provenance, replay and writer-serialization contracts.
frontier: Run the complete provenance runtime against the exact blob-pinned production sibling graph in one repository-local Python runtime; compare durable ADMIT/RESERVE/SLOT/COMMIT/CLOSE bytes and replay state with the injected-contract results.

Combine the provenance lifecycle with real multiprocessing: race two or more processes on the same ADMIT and same slot reservation under PosixFlockedCASAppendWriter, then race SLOT/CLOSE and COMMIT/CLOSE boundaries; require one reservation/one scorer attempt, stale-capability rejection, and exact final replay.

If deployment can span hosts or storage without reliable flock, design a monotonic fencing-token writer whose storage layer rejects stale fence values; do not generalize the single-host result to distributed execution.

Add a durable runtime manifest/pointer only after exact production-byte execution confirms the superseding runtime graph; until then treat these artifacts as validated candidate machinery rather than production authority.
